payload.comment:
Profiling stage is thorough and internally consistent. All split sizes (train 89 996 / val 10 004 / test 7 180) match the official PathMNIST manifest; no subsampling was applied; SHA-256 index hashes, archive MD5, and Zenodo reference are all recorded. The full dataset (107 180 samples) was profiled with zero blank images and zero duplicate train samples. Channel statistics, per-class counts/proportions for all three splits, train and test imbalance ratios, and test-to-train prevalence ratios are all computed and reported. The 28×28×3 image shape is correct for PathMNIST by design.

The data_profile correctly and prominently flags the key downstream risks: (1) substantial test-distribution shift relative to train/val (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56, smooth muscle ×0.61), (2) the external clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) introducing uncontrolled staining/scanner variability, (3) label ambiguity for 'debris', 'background', 'cancer-associated stroma' vs 'smooth muscle' at 28×28 patch resolution, (4) small per-class test counts (debris n=339, stroma n=421, smooth muscle n=592) making per-class metrics noisy, and (5) the near-identical train/val split confirming the test set is the sole external generalisation probe. These are inherent dataset characteristics, not profiling errors, and are well-documented for downstream stages.

Two inherited concerns from ingestion carry forward: llm_model_digest is null (reproducibility gap if the LLM is used downstream) and the model identifier 'qwen3.8' is atypical for the Qwen naming convention. Neither affects the profiling output, but both should be resolved before any LLM-dependent downstream stage.

No deterministic findings were raised. The profiling artefact is complete, well-structured, and ready to inform the next stage.
llm_issues: Inherited from ingestion: llm_model_digest is null; exact Qwen model revision cannot be verified or reproduced if the LLM is used in any downstream stage
Inherited from ingestion: llm_model identifier 'qwen3.8' is atypical for the Qwen naming convention; confirm it is the intended tag and not a typo

Test-set class distribution deviates substantially from train/val (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56, smooth muscle ×0.61); downstream evaluation must report per-class metrics with this shift explicitly noted
External clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) introduces uncontrolled H&E staining, scanner, and slide-preparation variability; downstream stages should include domain-shift-aware evaluation
Small per-class test counts (debris n=339, stroma n=421, smooth muscle n=592) make per-class test metrics statistically noisy; consider confidence intervals or bootstrap in reporting
Label ambiguity for 'debris', 'background', 'cancer-associated stroma' vs 'smooth muscle' at 28×28 patch resolution is a known limitation; downstream model selection should account for this
